messages:
Clara: Heads-up — customer reported a console spike where a single streaming request showed two confirmed lines for ~4s after a resume + toolcall. trace=trc_y9f, sess=ss_210. Tagging @Omar (router) and @Jess (metering).

Omar: timeline?

Clara: client opened stream -> sent 75-token prefix -> transient network drop -> client reconnects with resume_key -> router handoff to a different worker -> during resume a toolcall executes -> model returns EOF/truncated -> ledger shows two provisional claims (both 37 tokens) with identical prefix hash then two confirms, later consolidation reconciled to single usage and a refund was emitted. Customer received an automated quota alert during the window.

Jess: ledger snippet (sanitized):
```
[2026-04-21T16:02:01Z] ledger: provisional id=p_77 trace=trc_y9f sess=ss_210 tokens=37 hash=0x7c2a
[2026-04-21T16:02:04Z] router: handoff worker-3 -> worker-9
[2026-04-21T16:02:04Z] ledger: provisional id=p_78 trace=trc_y9f sess=ss_210 tokens=37 hash=0x7c2a
[2026-04-21T16:02:05Z] toolcall: invoked name=tool_sync trace=trc_y9f parent_provisional=p_77
[2026-04-21T16:02:06Z] ledger: confirm p_77 -> c_500 tokens=37
[2026-04-21T16:02:07Z] ledger: confirm p_78 -> c_501 tokens=37
[2026-04-21T16:02:10Z] reconcile: merge c_500,c_501 -> c_500 tokens=37 (refund issued)
```

Omar: likely root cause: router handoff didn't propagate resume_key/parent_provisional so ledger created a new provisional on the resumed connection.

Clara: customers get worried when the console shows two confirmed lines then a refund. we should reduce transient churn.

Jess: options: (1) router: forward resume_key + parent_provisional headers on handoff (prevents most cases), (2) ledger: add confirm-coalesce: on confirm, check for other provisional ids with same prefix hash in 10s window and atomically confirm earliest + tombstone others (set suppress_refund flag and record merged_ids), (3) console: collapse provisional duplicates and show "merged provisional events" badge linking to trace.

Omar: tradeoffs: (1) is best long-term but touches routing metadata widely. (2) is a safe safety-net and low-risk to roll out. (3) improves UX quickly but doesn't stop backend churn/alarms. I vote 2+3, then follow-up 1.

Jess: implementation notes: confirm-coalesce will use a provisional-hash key in the kv-store and CAS to elect the confirmer to avoid race confirms. When tombstoning extras, set `suppress_refund=true` in billing emission to avoid duplicate refund flows. Add `merged_ids` metadata to confirmed record so console can link.

Clara: UX: collapse provisional rows when hashes match and timestamps within grace window (default 15s). show tooltip: "These provisional charges were merged during reconciliation" and link to raw trace. add console filter to show only confirmed charges.

InfraBot: Canary scheduled: ledger/confirm-coalesce -> 2026-04-22T03:00Z (canary: us-west-2 low-traffic). Router header-forward patch planned for 2026-04-24.

Omar: I'll prototype router header pass-through and coordinate canary after ledger patch.

Jess: I'll open ledger PR with unit tests for concurrent confirms and a replay sim. Clara: please coordinate the console mock.

Clara: will do. I'll update this thread with PR links and canary metrics: provisional_merge_rate, transient_confirm_rows, refunds_suppressed. :thumbsup:
